title: Figurative Language
description: Using comparisons and images to make writing more vivid and expressive.

notes.heading: Simile and Metaphor
notes.body: Simile: compares using "like" or "as" ("Her smile was like sunshine"). Metaphor: direct comparison without "like/as" ("Her smile was sunshine"). Metaphors feel more powerful because they state something IS something else.

notes.heading: Personification and Hyperbole
notes.body: Personification: gives human qualities to non-human things ("The wind whispered"). Hyperbole: deliberate exaggeration ("I've told you a million times!").

notes.heading: Onomatopoeia and Alliteration
notes.body: Onomatopoeia: words that sound like the thing (buzz, crash, sizzle). Alliteration: repetition of initial consonant sounds ("Peter Piper picked"). Both create rhythm and emphasis.

flashcards.example: "The boy ran as fast as a cheetah."
